paper_title: Memorization and Knowledge Injection in Gated LLMs
caption: Analysis on the embedding quality in Llama intermediate layers. Correct gate rate is computed as the rate of question embeddings which have the maximum inner product with the relevant passage embedding. It is computed for each dataset partition, which has 50 passage samples. Shaded area is the standard deviation across 20 dataset partitions. We found that embeddings at the input of MLP layers are better than at the input of attention layers. We choose to use last MLP layer input as embedding in the main experiments of MEGa.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the average correct gate rate across embedding layers for different input types. The x-axis, labeled "Embedding Layer," is on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 30, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Average Correct Gate Rate," is also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.2 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The plot features four lines: a solid blue line representing "Character Attention input," a dashed blue line representing "Character MLP input," a solid red line representing "Wiki Attention input," and a dashed red line representing "Wiki MLP input." Each line has a shaded area indicating the standard deviation across 20 dataset partitions. The solid blue line starts at approximately 0.3 and increases to around 0.8 at layer 5, then decreases to about 0.4 at layer 10, before increasing again to around 0.7 at layer 30. The dashed blue line starts at approximately 0.8 and remains relatively stable around 0.8-0.9 across the embedding layers. The solid red line starts at approximately 0.4 and increases to around 0.7 at layer 15, then fluctuates between 0.6 and 0.7. The dashed red line starts at approximately 0.8 and remains relatively stable around 0.8-0.9 across the embedding layers.
